newsitem.title: POLAND: US, Polish firms to build power plant in Poland.
newsitem.headline: US, Polish firms to build power plant in Poland.

text.p: The U.S.'s Southern Electric International -- a subsidiary of Southern Co -- and a Polish electric power firm plan to build a modern power and heat generating plant in Poland worth up to $80 million.

The president of the Polish firm Ryszard Rabiega told Reuters on Tuesday that the two firms had set up a company in which the Polish firm, Zaklad Energetyczny Zamosc SA, had 51 percent and Southern Electric 49 percent.
The new firm will build Poland's first power and heat generating plant to use gas as its energy source.
"The cost of the investment, which will be financed from bank credit, is estimated at between $70 million and $80 million," Rabiega said.
He said the project in Zamosc, southeastern Poland, would start next year and that the plant was expected to be ready in 1998 or 1999.
